newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon aims for higher agricultural output.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon aims for higher agricultural output.

text.p: Lebanon's agriculture minister said in remarks published on Saturday that the country would launch a plan to boost annual agricultural growth to 20 percent from the current seven percent over the next three years.

Shawki Fakhoury was quoted by Beirut newspapers as saying the plan would include modern irrigation schemes, expected to increase irrigated lands by 30 percent, the planting of 1,500 acres (about 600 hectares) of forests annually, a rise in the number of plant nurseries to 13 from nine, and loans to small farmers.

Lebanon, seeking to slash the $1 billion annual food and vegetable import bill, has said it will halt as of October 1 the import of agricultural products that can be homegrown in an attempt to boost productivity and activate the agro-industry.

In 1996, Lebanon imported food and vegetables worth $1.058 billion, 14 percent of its total imports of $7.559 billion, while it exported $132 million worth of these products, 13 percent of the total $1.018 exports bill.
